DonorDock is generally the better fit if you want **one simple, all-in-one nonprofit CRM** with **unlimited contacts**, bundled email/text/online giving, and action-oriented task guidance. Bloomerang is usually the stronger choice if you want **deeper retention analytics**, built-in data quality tools, and broader nonprofit ecosystem features, even though pricing can scale with contacts and some modules may be separate. [1][7]

| Category | DonorDock | Bloomerang |
|---|---|---|
| Best for | Smaller/lean nonprofits that want simplicity and daily action focus | Nonprofits that prioritize retention analytics and donor intelligence |
| Pricing model | One plan with unlimited contacts, no contracts [1][2] | Pricing scales with contacts; some modules/add-ons are separate [1][7] |
| Core strengths | CRM, email, text messaging, online giving, project boards, AI assistant in one plan [1] | Donor engagement scoring, wealth screening, address verification, deceased suppression, data hygiene [7] |
| Workflow style | ActionBoard/Smart Nudges focus on “what to do today” [1] | Focuses more on reporting, scoring, and analytics [1][7] |
| Volunteer tools | More limited; can integrate with a dedicated volunteer platform for more advanced needs [7] | More robust native volunteer management, though priced separately in some cases [7] |

A few practical takeaways:

- Choose **DonorDock** if your team is small, wants fewer system decisions, and values straightforward day-to-day execution over advanced analytics. [1][7]
- Choose **Bloomerang** if donor retention, engagement scoring, and data hygiene are central to your fundraising strategy. [1][7]
- If your database is growing quickly, Bloomerang’s contact-based pricing may become more expensive over time, while DonorDock’s unlimited-contact pricing stays predictable. [1][2]

If you want, I can also give you a **“which one should we pick?” recommendation** based on your nonprofit’s size, budget, and must-have features.
